detailed_results.question: Why do veins appear blue?
detailed_results.answer: Veins appear blue due to the way light is absorbed and reflected by the skin and blood vessels beneath the surface. When light hits the skin, it is mostly absorbed by the tissues but some of it is reflected back towards the surface. The blood in veins absorbs more red and green wavelengths than it reflects, so when it's reflected back through the skin, it appears blue.
